title: What does the evidence say about nickel in people?

grade.title: At least one good randomized trial, or consistent human evidence from more than one source
grade.outcome: Oral nickel, including flare in sensitised people
grade.basis: EFSA published a chronic tolerable daily intake and identified oral flare in sensitised people. IARC classifies nickel compounds in Group 1. Not graded A.

answerHtml: EFSA in 2020 set a chronic tolerable daily intake of 13 µg nickel per kg body weight per day. Allergic contact dermatitis is the effect EFSA used for oral flare in sensitised people, as recorded from that opinion. EPA's oral reference dose for soluble nickel salts is 0.02 mg/kg/day, last updated in 1991, and it did not estimate a cancer value.

sections.heading: Reference values
sections.html:
EFSA in 2020, recorded in the corpus as checked against the opinion, set a tolerable daily intake of 13 µg/kg body weight per day, replacing a 2015 value of 2.8 µg/kg/day. The corpus records allergic contact dermatitis as the most common effect and systemic eczematous flare after oral exposure in sensitised people as the acute reference-point endpoint. A WHO drinking-water value of 70 µg/L is recorded as cited in that EFSA opinion. EFSA 2020.

EPA IRIS, last updated 1 December 1991, lists an oral reference dose of 2 x 10^-2 mg/kg/day for soluble nickel salts, based on decreased body and organ weights. The cancer assessment says the information was reviewed but a value was not estimated. EPA IRIS nickel.

The corpus records ATSDR 2024 inhalation minimal risk levels of 0.0001 mg Ni/m3 (acute) and 0.000003 mg Ni/m3 (intermediate), checked against the 2024 profile, which is not in the saved sources folder. ATSDR toxicological profiles. IARC, as cited there, places nickel compounds in Group 1 and metallic nickel in Group 2B. IARC volume 100C. Oral absorption details were not re-extracted.
